wire.providers.connect.key_invalid_chara.note: Shown under the API-key field when the pasted key holds spaces, line breaks or non-ASCII characters (usually a copy-paste accident). The key was NOT saved.

wire.providers.connect.key_rejected.note: Shown when the provider refused the pasted API key on a test request; the key was NOT saved. {label} is the provider's company or product name (e.g. 'Google', 'OpenAI'), never translated.

wire.providers.connect.key_unreachable.note: Shown when the test request could not reach the provider (offline, proxy, timeout). The key WAS saved, just not verified. {label} is the provider's name, never translated.

wire.providers.connect.key_unverified.note: Shown when the provider answered the test request with a status that says nothing definite about the key (rate limit, outage, region block). The key WAS saved, just not verified. {label} is the provider's name; {status} is the numeric HTTP status code (e.g. 429): keep 'HTTP {status}' as a technical token.

wire.providers.connect.suggested_automat.note: Display name of Radient's router model, which picks a model per request. Shown where a provider's suggested default model is named, e.g. 'Suggests Automatic' in the connect-provider list and 'Default model set to Automatic'. An adjective/noun meaning 'chosen automatically'.
